title: Loan-to-Value Allowance on the Comprehensive Deductible for Faxed Proof Re-Reviews — Collateral Protection Insurance Q&A
content:
**Rule.** In the re-review of a faxed proof under Collateral Protection Insurance on a closed tracking record, the ceiling for the proof's comprehensive deductible is raised by a loan-to-value allowance: USD 500.00 when the amount financed was no more than 100 percent of the vehicle book value at signing, and USD 250.00 when it was above 100 percent and no more than 120 percent. Above 120 percent there is an allowance of USD 0.00.

## Questions and answers

**Which figures does the loan-to-value use?** Both come from the borrower's Retail Installment Contracts record: the amount financed disclosed at signing, and the vehicle book value used for loan-to-value at origination. The loan-to-value is the amount financed divided by that book value, expressed as a percent.

**A contract financed exactly 100 percent of book value. Which raise applies?** USD 500.00: "no more than 100 percent" includes 100 percent itself.

**And at 100.5 percent?** USD 250.00, being above 100 percent and no more than 120 percent.

**At exactly 120 percent?** USD 250.00. At 120.1 percent there is an allowance of USD 0.00.

**Does this allowance touch the collision deductible?** No. It raises only the comprehensive deductible's ceiling.

## Hypothetical figures

| Amount financed (USD) | Book value at signing (USD) | Loan-to-value | Raise to the comprehensive ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9000.00 | 10000.00 | 90 percent | USD 500.00 |
| 11000.00 | 10000.00 | 110 percent | USD 250.00 |
| 13000.00 | 10000.00 | 130 percent | USD 0.00 |
